falsification_pass_summary: H1 was the only hypothesis whose premise could be tested with data already in hand, and it failed its own test. H2 was then implemented and is the shipped field. H3 is metric arithmetic and is shipped with it. H4, H5, H6 are registered with named free official sources and each source's measured reachability from this sandbox recorded above. H9 falsified against 19 reported scores (mass correlated -0.653 with score).

hypotheses.cost: low (implemented and falsified in ~4 minutes of CPU)
hypotheses.differs_from_prior_work: Every placement prior in this project family (proximity exp(-d/1km), EDGE(external), EDGE(hybrid)) is an ISOTROPIC radial kernel of distance-to-catalogue. H1 was the anisotropic alternative.
hypotheses.falsification_test: scripts/measure_population.py, registry/population.json: offset-angle histogram for SGMC-only fault pixels versus a distance-matched random footprint control, both sampled from the 1.5-9 px band from the catalogue. Result: SGMC 0.102 within 30 deg of strike / 0.736 within 30 deg of across-strike / median 74.8 deg; control 0.100 / 0.742 / 75.2 deg. Enrichment per 15 deg bin: SGMC 0.31 0.31 0.37 0.60 1.45 2.97 versus control 0.30 0.31 0.35 0.60 1.42 3.03.
layers: labels.tif (competition catalogue) - only as a strike/geometry source
no feature band required
hypotheses.physical_signature: Offset vector from a non-catalogue fault pixel to the nearest catalogue pixel, expressed in the local catalogue strike frame. The claim was that new geometry of an existing system sits preferentially ACROSS strike (parallel splays, relay ramps, hanging-wall strands) rather than isotropically around the trace.
hypotheses.status: FALSIFIED by measurement before any submission slot
hypotheses.title: Strike-frame offset-strand synthesis (anisotropic across-strike placement prior)
hypotheses.verdict: The apparent across-strike preference is a distance-transform artefact (for a random point near a line, the nearest point on the line is nearly always perpendicular to it). There is NO measurable anisotropy signal beyond that geometric baseline, so the anisotropic kernel cannot be justified. Hypothesis dropped; no slot spent.
hypotheses.why_it_should_be_missing_from_the_catalo: A catalogue records where rock is exposed enough to map a trace; a parallel strand one valley-width away, or a relay ramp between two en-echelon segments, is systematically under-recorded even when the main trace is mapped.

hypotheses.cost: medium (CPU only, ~15 minutes per 4-fold run on 2 vCPU)
hypotheses.data_obtainability: SGMC raster is obtainable and hash-verified in this sandbox via `gh api repos/buffedlizard55-lab/GEMSDOE24/contents/data/external/derived_sgmc_faults_100m_u8.tif` (198,602 B, sha256 643cbe992ef4ba37...).
hypotheses.differs_from_prior_work: Prior repositories in this family (GEMSDOE19/24/25/27/28/32/33) rank and promote candidates on frames whose truth IS the catalogue, and GEMSDOE32 measured that such frames rank artifacts in the OPPOSITE order to the live board (0.17193 > 0.16635 > 0.16177 catalogue-proxy versus live 0.1922 < 0.2477 < 0.2600). This repo trains the field itself on the off-catalogue population and promotes only on that frame. GEMSDOE29 registered an 'sgmc-off-catalogue-44k' artifact but never obtained a score for it; no prior repo reports a spatially blocked off-catalogue AUC or uses that frame for model selection.
hypotheses.expected_dti: positive; measured on the off-catalogue frame in registry/holdout.json

hypotheses.physical_signature: Supervised P(a pixel lies on a mapped fault that the competition catalogue does not contain), learned from named multi-scale transforms (raw value, 3x3 mean, 9x9 mean, Laplacian curvature at 3 and 9 px).
hypotheses.status: IMPLEMENTED AND VALIDATED - this is the shipped field
hypotheses.title: Off-catalogue supervised field: the competition catalogue is the wrong training target
hypotheses.why_it_should_catch_a_catalogue_missing_: It is trained on real mapped faults that ARE absent from the given catalogue, so the discriminative direction it learns is the direction that separates catalogue-absent from catalogue-present terrain. Measured evidence that this matters: the discriminative SIGN of several bands flips between the two populations. Univariate AUC for detrended_elevation_slope_m3 is 0.747 for SGMC-only faults but only 0.561 for catalogue faults; geodetic_2nd_invariant is 0.478 for SGMC-only versus 0.560 for catalogue. A model trained on the catalogue therefore learns partly the wrong direction.

hypotheses.differs_from_prior_work: GEMSDOE30/32 implemented an expected-marginal-credit emitter (EDGE) but only ever swept the thinning radius at 1.5 and 2.8 px and reported the emission side as 'nearly used up'. This repo emits on a field whose belief is an off-catalogue probability, and derives the mass from leave-one-fold-out selection on the off-catalogue frame plus the closed-form break-even condition.
hypotheses.expected_dti: +0.005 to +0.025 on the off-catalogue frame versus a raster-order thinning cascade at matched mass, mechanism measured in registry/holdout.json
layers: none: this is metric arithmetic, not data
hypotheses.physical_signature: Not a physical signature. The official metric's TP term is a MAX over a 300 m disc, so expected credit is submodular in the emitted set and fixed-order greedy carries the standard (1 - 1/e) guarantee. The first-order stopping condition is k > alpha * DTI, i.e. a dot pays iff its kernel credit exceeds 20 percent of the current score.
hypotheses.status: IMPLEMENTED - shipped inside the H2 artifact
hypotheses.title: Metric-exact marginal-credit emission at the analytic mass
hypotheses.why_it_matters: Raster-order thinning cascades (the family's 'dot_thin') suppress by distance in raster order and can delete a dot that is the only cover of a scored truth pixel while keeping a redundant one.

hypotheses.cost: medium-high (multi-scale filtering over a 36.9 MB derived raster plus 1 m tile mosaicking)
hypotheses.data_obtainability: The derived scarp raster IS obtainable from this sandbox via the hash-pinned mirror. The raw 3DEP 1 m tiles are NOT reachable from this sandbox: prd-tnm.s3.amazonaws.com and earthexplorer.usgs.gov both returned HTTP 000 (connection failure) on a direct test on 2026-10-06.
hypotheses.differs_from_prior_work: GEMSDOE7 shipped a lidar-scarp ranking at 0.1461 and GEMSDOE24 stores the derived scarp raster, but no prior repo in this family runs a coupled ridge-trough dipole detector with strike-consistency gating and validates it on the off-catalogue frame.
hypotheses.expected_dti: positive but unmeasured here; the field would be added as an extra feature to H2
layers: USGS 3DEP 1 m DEM tiles (external)
the owner-derived derivative raster data/external/lidar_scarp_features_u8.tif (36,943,606 B, hash-pinned in the GEMSDOE24 mirror)
hypotheses.physical_signature: A fault scarp is a step in the surface whose second derivative is a paired ridge and trough; the separation between the pair encodes scarp width and height. A matched filter for that dipole, at multiple scales and azimuths with strike-consistency gating, detects scarps whose wavelength is below the 100 m competition grid.
hypotheses.status: REGISTERED - NOT RUN; data partially obtainable
hypotheses.title: Coupled ridge-trough (curvature dipole) matched filter on 1 m lidar
hypotheses.why_it_should_catch_a_catalogue_missing_: The metric's FP tax is 0.2 per unit while FN costs 0.8, so a scarp that is real but subtle is worth predicting. A 5 m scarp over 20 m of ground is invisible in a 100 m band but is exactly the kind of feature an expert adds when they work from lidar.

hypotheses.data_obtainability: Both CSVs and the SGMC raster are obtainable and hash-verified from this sandbox via the GEMSDOE24 mirror.
hypotheses.differs_from_prior_work: GEMSDOE32 measured that GDR QFaults v2 adds nothing on its own (59,064 of its 59,065 rasterised pixels lie within 300 m of the given catalogue), so its information is entirely in the SGMC half of the union; this repo would use the union with the disagreement explicitly modelled rather than as a proximity kernel.
hypotheses.expected_dti: moderate; likely correlated with H2 and therefore partly redundant

USGS SGMC rasterised faults (198,602 B, hash-pinned)

hypotheses.physical_signature: Distance to the nearest fault that appears in some public official compilation but NOT in the given catalogue, gated by the metric's credit bar.
hypotheses.title: Cross-compilation disagreement as a gated feature
hypotheses.why_it_should_catch_a_catalogue_missing_: It is the only source of KNOWN REAL faults that the given catalogue lacks, so it targets the right population by construction rather than by inference.

hypotheses.data_obtainability: NOT obtainable from this sandbox: earthquake.usgs.gov returned HTTP 000 (connection failure) on a direct test on 2026-10-06, reproducing the block reported by GEMSDOE32.
hypotheses.differs_from_prior_work: GEMSDOE32 registered this as H33-E and reported it data-blocked after measuring that the supplied seismic bands carry no fault-scale information (autocorrelation of ieq_n100a15 = 0.9986 at 1 km and 0.9935 at 3 km).

official band 16 earthquake intensity/density as the in-competition surrogate
hypotheses.physical_signature: A lineament of relocated hypocentres, not a density field. The official band 16 is a smoothed density with n=100 km and a=15 deg parameters; it cannot express a fault-scale lineament.
hypotheses.status: REGISTERED - NOT RUN; data NOT obtainable from this sandbox
hypotheses.title: Relocated-seismicity lineament skeletons from the raw USGS FDSN catalogue
hypotheses.why_it_should_catch_a_catalogue_missing_: Small earthquakes delineate active structures that a surface catalogue may miss, particularly where the trace is buried.

hypotheses.differs_from_prior_work: The family decimated rasters to reach 44,090 dots (d2.8 thinning, Poisson); this solves the coverage problem directly by marginal expected credit on the accepted set, and verifies zero 8-adjacency in the shipped file.
hypotheses.expected_dti: adds the difference between a clumped and a spaced emission of the same field; on the family's own history that difference was 0.26 vs 0.19 at 2.75x the mass.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Ship or score it against the incumbent at matched density on the blocked folds; check 8-adjacency = 0 and that it never loses to a raster-prefix emission.
layers: all 19 official bands (the field it is applied to)
hypotheses.physical_signature: metric arithmetic: a dot's credit is max_x k(d(x,g)); a dot 8-adjacent to another adds ~no new truth coverage while each dot pays alpha=0.2 of FP.
hypotheses.title: Exact greedy max-coverage emission at the metric's own spacing (adjacent dots are forbidden)
hypotheses.verdict: Supported descriptively at n=19: the three best reported artifacts have 0.001-0.002 adjacent-dot fractions vs 0.88-0.99 for low scorers; Spearman(live, adjacent fraction) = -0.361.
hypotheses.why_it_should_be_missing_from_the_catalo: It is an emission rule, not a field: it decides WHERE mass goes without changing what is believed, and dots on catalogue pixels are deleted by the mask, so it can only earn credit on unmapped truth.

hypotheses.differs_from_prior_work: The family's best surfaces are h19-5 (proprietary opacity/thermal prior) and ridge/scarp detectors. h18-4 'usgs-geologic-map-faults-gap' scored 0.0360 live, but used map-gap evidence directly with a dense clumped emission and no supervised transfer.
hypotheses.expected_dti: unknown; gate requires >= +0.005 over the 0.2600 incumbent.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Blocked-fold emission on frames N and P against the incumbent at matched density; fails if it cannot beat the incumbent on frame N.

hypotheses.physical_signature: supervised classification: positives = SGMC strand pixels absent from the competition catalogue and within 300 m of it (17,493 px), negatives = background; the same construction on the wider SGMC residual reached blocked AUC 0.773 (folds 0.762-0.789).
hypotheses.title: Supervised transfer of the USGS SGMC compilation onto the official feature stack, trained on catalogue-adjacent unmapped strands
hypotheses.why_it_should_be_missing_from_the_catalo: The positives ARE mapped faults the competition catalogue lacks - the only locally available analogue of the hidden label set; the catalogue's own pixels are the mask and are never predicted.

hypotheses.differs_from_prior_work: GEMSDOE22 h23-a 'dti-optimal-emission-6pct' emitted 335,879 dots (6% of pixels) and scored 0.1002 live.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Correlate reported score with dot count across 19 scored artifacts.
hypotheses.title: Dense emission is better because beta=0.8 weights FN four times FP
hypotheses.verdict: Falsified: Spearman(live, mass) = -0.653. The optimum is where the marginal dot's expected credit equals 0.2*DTI, not at maximum mass.

ranking_metric: expected DTI gain per unit of implementation cost, judged after the falsification pass
required_fields_note: Each entry names (a) the specific layer(s), (b) the physical signature targeted, (c) why it should catch a fault MISSING from the USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue rather than one already in it, (d) how it differs from everything already implemented in this repo, (e) expected DTI direction and implementation cost, (f) the free official data source and its measured obtainability from this sandbox.
